title: Preparation of Flame Retardant Cotton Fabric Using Environmental Friendly Supercritical Carbon Dioxide

treatment_method: Immerse cotton in 50% aqueous isopropanol containing flame retardant and pad at 10 psi. Treat in supercritical CO2 at 90 C for 2 h under 1800-2000 psi. Dry at 100 C for 5 min and cure at 160 C for 4 min.
source_title: Preparation of Flame Retardant Cotton Fabric Using Environmental Friendly Supercritical Carbon Dioxide
source_location: Original article sections 2.4-2.5 and 3.2-3.4; Table 2.
limitations: Exact nitrogen R600 is used. Table 2 multi-stage onsets are retained source-native and are not relabeled as DTG maxima. ASTM edition conflict is preserved, with no inferred correction. Untreated control has only a generic LOI range and inconsistent residue prose, so it is excluded. Air mentioned in introduction has no separate reported numerical TG condition. Original article text was accessed on Scribd; publisher PDF bytes were unavailable. No PDF pixel review claimed.

TGA_preconditioning: Heat from room temperature to 100 C at 10 C/min; hold for 20 min; then the stated 10 or 20 C/min ramp to 600 C.

treatment_chemistry: Fyrol 76 vinyl phosphonate oligomer (FYR) and/or N-methylolacrylamide (NMA), ammonium persulfate initiated
treatment_method: Base fabric cleaned using 0.2% anionic surfactant, then ethanol/benzene (1:1) Soxhlet extraction and air drying. Pad with aqueous FYR/NMA bath and ammonium persulfate at 10% of monomer weight; approximately 80% pickup. Air dry, steam at 100 C for 10 min, air dry, wash in distilled water at 80 C for 30 min, vacuum dry and store over silica gel.
source_title: Pad-Steam Treatments of Cotton Fabrics with Vinyl Phosphonate Oligomers and/or N-Methylolacrylamide and Thermal Behavior of the Treated Fabrics
source_location: Original Japanese article pp 272-277; Tables 1-3 and experimental sections 2.1-2.5.
limitations: Original publisher PDF methods and Tables 1-3 visually reviewed. NMA-4 LOI conflicts (21.4 table versus 21.5 prose) and remains held. DTA endotherm/exotherm peaks are not DTG maxima. Authors To/Tf describe main weight-loss boundaries, not T5/T10; only unambiguous TG Tmax/R600 included. Grafting-efficiency formula is not recalculated. Initial thermal prehold is not aging or laundering. Two ramps count as one state.
journal: Journal of the Japan Research Association for Textile End-Uses
LOI_locator: Table 1, p 273, exact sample-code LOI. Untreated LOI 18.6 is explicitly stated in the table footnote.
LOI_method: Source reports JIS L7201 and Suga ON-1 oxygen index instrument; identifier retained verbatim without a compliance claim.
TG_locator: Table 3, p 277, 20 C/min: TG Tmax and residue at 600 C; DTA columns excluded.
conditions_locator: Section 2.5, p 273: nitrogen 30 mL/min, 100 C prehold for 20 min, then 10 or 20 C/min to 600 C; approximate 7 mg fabric aliquots.
pairing_evidence: Exact untreated/FYR/NMA/F/N sample codes link preparation and LOI Table 1 to both TG Tables 2/3. Two TG ramps are repeat conditions of one prepared material state, not extra samples. Preparative hot-water extraction is not a durability-wash series.
TGA_instrument: Shimadzu DTG-50 simultaneous TG-DTA; TA-50WS processing

treatment_method: Original kombucha BC was washed, bleached and swollen according to cited protocols; upstream recipe is not repeated. Dissolve 50 wt% anchovy powder relative to BC in distilled water at BC:liquid 1:10 w/v. Add citric acid at 10% w/v and sodium hypophosphite at crosslinker:catalyst molar ratio 1:1. Stir at 25 +/-2 C for 30 min, adjust to pH 10.0 +/-0.5 with 1 N NaOH, and denature at 80 C for 20 min with shaking at 80 rpm. Cool to 25 +/-2 C; immerse BC, ultrasonicate at 25 C for 30 min, shake at 30 C for 1 h at 80 rpm, cure at 160 C for 5 min and dry at 25 C for 24 h.

treatment_method: Disperse MTMOS in 100 mL distilled water with surfactants using a FA25 FLUKO disperser. Acid-hydrolyze for 4 h, then add TEOS dropwise and react for 2 h; modify the sol with HDTMS. Source optimization identifies 1.5 g MTMOS, 2.5 g TEOS, CTAC:Tween 60 = 2:3, surfactant dosage 0.9% (denominator unstated), pH 3 and 30 °C synthesis. cot_Si is explicitly pure silica hydrosol, without ammonium biphosphate; HDTMS amount and the exact cot_Si-specific quantities are not separately stated. Pad at 2 kg/cm² nip pressure, dry at 80 °C for 5 min and cure for 5 min; optimization captions specify 130 °C. Condition at 25 ± 2 °C and 65% humidity for 24 h. No durability washing reported.

treatment_method: Prepare aqueous UV-curable formulation at source-labelled 100% TMEP application, with Darocur 1173 (2-hydroxy-2-methyl-1-phenylpropan-1-one) at 7 wt% of monomer and Triton X-100 1 g/L. Dip and pad to 90% wet pickup; dry at 80 C for 3 min in Daelim laboratory tenter. Irradiate each face at 0.8 J/cm2 using an 80 W/cm continuous UV machine. Preparation includes water rinse, documented by W3 after-rinse mass; rinse parameters and post-rinse drying are not stated. Exact monomer synthesis stoichiometry/time/temperature are not reported in this paper.
source_title: Flame-retardant Finish of Cotton Fabrics Using UV-curable Phosphorous-containing Monomers
source_location: Complete original seven-page Korean journal PDF downloaded and text-reviewed. Exact Tables 1-3 and preparation/method paragraphs independently read from page images; no curve estimates.
limitations: No graph-derived values, inferred exact add-ons or inferred SD. Nominal application is source-labelled percent; its denominator is not explicitly assigned in the preparation paragraph, so it is not converted to bath wt%, owf or final fabric fraction. Source-native F and residue number are retained but not converted into add-on. First/second thermal-decomposition ranges are not formal onset thresholds or endpoints of the instrument; they remain source-native. DTGA peak temperatures support canonical Tmax1/Tmax2. Table 1 caption mentions TMEP alone but its rows and adjoining prose explicitly include both MMEP and TMEP. R800 is direct, not inferred from Nr. Initial water rinse is acknowledged, but its time, temperature and post-rinse drying are unstated. Durability cycles 1/3/5 have LOI only and remain held. Related 2007 DMEP cotton source shares control LOI18.4 and R8008.9 but has Tmax395 versus this source391; that older control is withheld from a future second draft pending reuse review. Related 2008 Fibers and Polymers DOI10.1007/s12221-008-0105-2 includes films and fabrics; no values are borrowed or extra states counted without exact original version review.

composition: 100% natural cotton fabric, 120 g/m², Texmar Company, Egypt. Weave and yarn specifications are not stated.
treatment_chemistry: PVA and melamine salt of tannic phosphate; Table 1 reports 10% PVA plus 30% MTP
treatment_method: Wash cotton fabric with deionized water and dry at 60 °C for 1 h before use. Disperse 30 g melamine in 500 mL methanol; add tannic phosphate solution dropwise over 30 min, maintain the hot plate at 120 °C and react for 6 h. Filter, wash with methanol, dry at room temperature for 72 h and grind to powder. The source states that the beaker containing deionized water and PVA was heated to 150 °C for 30 min using a hot plate with mechanical stirring at 650 rpm. Whether 150 °C is the actual solution temperature or the hotplate setting is unresolved. PVA molecular weight is 115000 g/mol and degree of polymerization 1700-1800. Add MTP to the PVA solution under continuous stirring at 70 °C; use the Table 1 C7 formulation of 10% PVA and 30% MTP. Soak fabric in the finishing solution at 70 °C for 10 min; pad three times to 90% pickup, dry at 100 °C for 5 min and cure at 160 °C for 3 min. No durability tap-water rinsing is assigned to the initial state.

source_version: Final published journal article and its official institutional supplementary material
source_onset_definition: Source Tdonset is the temperature at 97% mass remaining, excluding moisture. Stored source-native only; not converted to T5 or T10.
source_recipe_holds: Piperazine stoichiometry: main section 2.2.2 and SI prose say equimolar/1:1 TVPO:piperazine, while the main equation explanation says 2:3. No ratio is selected. washing_protocol: One accelerated wash operation simulating five home laundry cycles: sandwich a 152.4 × 50.8 mm specimen between two multifiber test fabrics and stitch the edges. Rinse three times with demineralized water, dry at 60 °C for 2 h and condition in standard atmosphere for 24 h before other characterization. SI-4 prepares three wash specimens per sample. The main and SI heading cite AATCC 61-1996; SI procedural text and silver durability prose cite AATCC 61-2013, so standard edition remains source-conflicted.

source_location: Official institutional 14-page final published PDF and 22-page supplement. Main p 4 methods and p 6 LOI Table 2; SI p 15 TG Table SI-5, pp 6-8 recipes and p 9 washing. Main method/LOI and SI method/TG pixels reviewed; no graph digitization.
limitations: Eight prepared textile/wash states with sixteen atmospheric TG conditions. All LOI rows are after five simulated home laundry cycles, not unwashed. Table 4 uses representative chemistry names and rounds TPTEPO LOI to 27.4; no add-on or label crosswalk is inferred from that comparison table. Source laundering standard editions conflict; explicit physical wash conditions are retained.
LOI_locator: Final article p 6, Table 2, exact Blank/S9/S10/S11/S12/S14/S15/SS1 rows and five-wash footnote. LOI mean of five specimens in section 2.2.6 p 4; ±0.2 from the Table 2 header.
LOI_method: ASTM D2863-97; FTT oxygen index apparatus; five specimens tested and mean reported.
TG_locator: Official supplement p 15, Table SI-5: source Tdonset, explicitly DTG-defined Tdmax and residue at 800 °C for nitrogen and air.
conditions_locator: Final article p 4, sections 2.1 and 2.2.2-2.2.6; SI pp 6-9, sections SI-3.3 through SI-4. TG: approximately 4 mg, 25-800 °C, N2 and air, total gas flow 50 mL/min, 10 °C/min. Wash procedure: SI p 9.
pairing_evidence: Main Table 2 explicitly reports fire tests after five wash cycles. SI-4 states rinsed, dried and conditioned washed samples precede other characterization and analysis. For each treated fabric, Table SI-5 TG repeats the exact phosphorus value and uncertainty in the post-five-wash Table 1/SI-3/SI-4 column and main LOI Table 2. Labels and P values jointly identify the same states. Blank appears in both assay tables; Table 2 all-samples wash footnote and shared characterization procedure apply. No 50-wash state or neat polymer is substituted.

treatment_chemistry: Table 1 and Table 2: DATPPO:ODA molar ratio 0:10, with stoichiometric s-BPDA. DATPPO is [2,5-bis(4-aminophenoxy)phenyl] diphenylphosphine oxide; PI-0 is the ODA/s-BPDA control.
treatment_method: s-BPDA dried overnight under vacuum at 260 °C. DATPPO and ODA reacted with a stoichiometric quantity of s-BPDA in DMAc under nitrogen at room temperature for 24 h; solids 15 wt% of total solution. PAA solution filtered and degassed, then dry-jet wet spun through a 50-hole spinneret of 0.12 mm hole diameter into water/DMAc 42:58 by volume. Filaments passed a washing bath and heating oven and were collected on winders. PAA fibers heated to 300 °C to form PI fibers, followed by drawing. Table 1 assigns the unprimed PI-0 through PI-6 series draft ratio 3.0 and draw ratio 1.6; draw temperature and residence time are not stated. DATPPO monomer synthesis is documented in the official three-page SI; no durability laundering is reported.

limitations: Only untreated wool and the 27.4% WG initial treated fabric have own TG. Table 1 and section 2 map this treated state to a nominal 30% ANPP solution, but the basis of that solution percentage is not stated; do not convert it to g/L or final material fraction. Table 2 uses 0 LCs for initial LOI; the preparation includes a flowing-water rinse, which is retained as a process wash. The later durability LOIs are not paired to baseline TG. LOI ± values and Table 1 WG ± values have no stated statistical definition or replicate count; no SD or n is invented. Five repetitions in the whiteness/tensile methods are not assigned to LOI or TG. The TG mass sentence explicitly says treated sample, so the control mass remains unspecified. LOI drying at 80 °C for 4 h is not silently assigned to TG. The source contains unrelated interpretation errors, including type I cellulose and L-glucose language for wool, a later 33.7% WG typo versus the defined 35.7% state, and a two-stage description of treated air degradation despite two tabulated rate peaks plus initial moisture loss; these are preserved as source limitations and not used to repair the numerical tables. The extracted PDF text layer contains an INVITED REVIEW PAPER white-text header artifact, invisible on the rendered first page. The body supplies its own Experimental section, original measured tables, and an ANPP row explicitly marked This work in Table 5; publication type is journal_article and only those own measurements are used. The synthesis prose mentions 200 mL of 5% KMnO4 solution for formaldehyde absorption without a clear apparatus arrangement; no alternate synthesis arrangement is inferred.

treatment_chemistry: Ammonium salt 1,3-propylene glycol diphosphate ester (APGDPE), with dicyandiamide catalyst
treatment_method: Synthesize APGDPE from 1,3-propylene glycol (0.100 mol, 7.765 g) and phosphoric acid (0.200 mol, 23.059 g) at 130 °C for 3 h with magnetic stirring; continuously add urea (0.200 mol, 12.012 g), heat at 170 °C for 2.5 h, purify with absolute ethanol, filter and oven-dry at 60 °C; yield approximately 88%. Dissolve APGDPE in distilled water to a 40 wt% bath and add dicyandiamide catalyst, whose amount is not reported. Immerse cotton at 70 °C for 40 min using a 1:20 fabric-mass to bath-volume ratio; pad through a nip to 120% wet pickup, cure at 180 °C for 5 min using an automatic continuous backing machine, rinse with running water and dry at 60 °C for 1 h. No additional precleaning or conditioning protocol is stated.

treatment_method: Synthesize APGDPE from 1,3-propylene glycol (0.100 mol, 7.765 g) and phosphoric acid (0.200 mol, 23.059 g) at 130 °C for 3 h with magnetic stirring; continuously add urea (0.200 mol, 12.012 g), heat at 170 °C for 2.5 h, purify with absolute ethanol, filter and oven-dry at 60 °C; yield approximately 88%. Dissolve APGDPE in distilled water to a 40 wt% bath and add dicyandiamide catalyst, whose amount is not reported. Immerse cotton at 70 °C for 40 min using a 1:20 fabric-mass to bath-volume ratio; pad through a nip to 120% wet pickup, cure at 180 °C for 5 min using an automatic continuous backing machine, rinse with running water and dry at 60 °C for 1 h. No additional precleaning or conditioning protocol is stated.

DSC melting/cold-crystallization temperatures and X-ray crystallinity are separate assays. Source acknowledges presenting material at the December2016 X-Ray Investigations of Polymer Structure conference; any later proceedings source needs a specific reuse check. source_location: Complete original nine-page publisher PDF, pp 1–9; methods, Tables 1–4, Figures 1–7, conclusion and all references reviewed. Original pages 2,3,5,6,7,8 inspected as pixels for recipes, conditions, numerical tables, TG profiles and identity.
limitations: Five initial source textile states represented by ten TG conditions, not ten distinct states. Table 4 measured LOI ± values are retained with unspecified uncertainty type; neither SD nor LOI replicate count is inferred. Three repeated measurements and averaging in the source relate to stiffness/air-permeability methods, not expressly to LOI. All R600 values are explicit Tables 2/3 values; the standalone hydrogel residue 34.1% belongs to a nontextile specimen and is excluded. The TC10 nitrogen row prints two T10 values, 228 and 321 °C, across its two stage lines; canonical T10 is blank for that condition, with both raw values retained. T50 and R600 remain independently reported. DTG table temperatures are retained in native fields without assigning canonical decomposition peaks, because first-stage fabric losses are attributed mainly to moisture and unreacted monomers and peak semantics are not independently defined. No stage weight loss is converted into residue. Both Figure 5 axes read Weight loss (%) although the traces descend from about100; the axis wording is preserved and no graph coordinates are used. Canonical TG scan endpoints are blank because methods do not state them; residue assessment is explicitly 600 °C. Air is assigned from the explicit method, Table 2 and Figure 5(a); prose says the untreated fabric is destroyed in an oxygen atmosphere but does not specify a separate pure-O2 assay. This raw wording is retained, not used as another condition or zero-residue claim. Nominal 10/20/30/40% BisMEP labels, introduction mole-ratio wording, source gram amounts and Table 1 mM entries are not mutually resolved; use source-native labels and entries without calculating a corrected loading or retained add-on. For the same 5 mg AAPH, standalone hydrogel synthesis reports 18.4 × 10⁻³ mM but fabric coating reports 1.84 × 10⁻³ mM; both are retained and no exponent or unit is repaired. Drying at 60 °C overnight belongs to standalone hydrogel synthesis, while fabric coating uses70 °C with unspecified duration. TC40L is a distinct after-home-laundry state with LOI 25 ± 0.2 and no corresponding TG; it is held. Source stiffness prose says decreases although its tabulated stiffness rises; this unrelated inconsistency is not used to alter TG or LOI. Source-supplied cotton is not assumed to have an unreported bleach, scour or weave. Numeric reuse search found one common untreated LOI 18/T10 319 in DOI 10.14504/ajr.8.3.5, but its other condition values, preparation and instrument differ; no shared measurement identity is asserted from that partial coincidence.
